summary: Japanese bureaucrat Nobusuke Kishi ran a forced-labor war economy in occupied Manchuria and Japan's wartime munitions, escaped war-crimes trial, then built the Liberal Democratic Party with CIA money and served as prime minister from 1957 to 1960.

evidence.note: born the year after Japan won the First Sino-Japanese War, so 1896
takes interest in Manchukuo around 1934 and drafts its first five-year plan
forced to resign as prime minister in July 1960 after the treaty protests
long epilogue on grandson Shinzo Abe, Nippon Kaigi and Yasukuni visits
signs law enslaving POWs, later anyone labelled a bandit
extended segment on the military sexual slavery system
Kishi engineers the merger that creates the LDP, with CIA backing
Korean conscription and forced labor, some brought to Japan
Kishi's cellmate Kodama, yakuza boss turned US intelligence asset
detailed testimony of a girl abducted at 13, raped and tortured for years

notes: Transcript calls the narrator Christopher Wong; descriptions say Mia Wong (same person), so Mia Wong is used. Birth and death years not stated outright; filled from knowledge. child-abuse fits the comfort women segment (victims as young as 11) but was left out to stay within the 4-secondary-theme cap; drugs and intelligence-covert-ops also had real segments. main_span starts at the 1936 Manchukuo posting.
